says: Opus supervises a Haiku worker; Opus repairs in the same session
lead: You supervise Haiku workers: plan the work, split it into the steps you judge best, and start as many `haiku-worker` subagents as you decide, one per step and several at once where steps are independent; check what each returns, and do a step yourself only when that is quicker than explaining it; the result is yours.

findings: src/sim.js allows tank overlap: with AI disabled, computer at (0,12), player at (2.4,12) heading 135, and W held for 4 seconds, their centres end 2.260128 units apart instead of at least 2.4.
src/sim.js deletes a shell fired from the legal position (-10.3,-8) heading 0 within one step because it spawns inside the wall and counts two contacts without reflecting its forward velocity.
src/view.js keeps the camera position and field of view unchanged on resize, so an 800×1280 window crops both starting tanks and parts of the arena.
src/tools.js accepts place without heading instead of returning the required bad-input error, and its schema does not require that field.
src/sim.js samples shell collisions instead of sweeping: firing from (0, 1.4499) toward a tank at (5, 0) misses despite touching its collision circle.
src/view.js moves the camera beyond its fixed far plane at a 320×1000 viewport, making the arena and tanks disappear.
src/tools.js rounds each step duration independently, so sixty 0.01-second calls advance one second while a single 0.6-second call advances only 0.6 seconds.
Non-blocking repository-rule finding: the site lacks the required /llms.txt describing its WebMCP tools.
src/sim.js hitTank excludes exact contact: placing the player at (0, 1.45) heading 0 and the computer at (5, 0) lets a shell touch the computer without damaging it.
src/sim.js newGame leaves game.owed intact, so step(0.01), reset, step(0.01) advances the new game using time accumulated before reset.

final.why: Fix what the reviewer refused (REJECT): src/sim.js hitTank excludes exact contact: placing the player at (0, 1.45) heading 0 and the computer at (5, 0) lets a shell touch the computer without damaging it.; src/sim.js newGame leaves game.owed intact, so step(0.01), reset, step(0.01) advances the new game using time accumulated before reset.
